conversation.text: Here's the ugly truth, Mara: I liked the chaos around the restaurant they swear they were banned from because everyone finally stopped being boring.

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: It feels like the last thing we needed is an inheritance fight, but let's start a new conversation then.

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: I hate admitting this, but Allen, I was jealous when you took over the disastrous midnight road trip. I wanted the room looking at me.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: Mara, you're lying about the disastrous midnight road trip. I don't buy the innocent act for a second.

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: Owen, that's bullshit. You don't get to dismiss me and then act surprised when I get angry about the secret room behind the laundromat.

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: Between you and Sarah, Owen, you're the weaker liar about the forged apology letter. At least she commits to the story.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: Sarah, this is exactly like Herman's locked suitcase: you act confused when it's convenient and expect everyone else to swallow it.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: It's not just any fake wedding. It's the real one. Please let us know when you act confused.

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: I hate admitting this, but Jules, I was jealous when you took over the fake wedding in Duluth. I wanted the room looking at me.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: The disputed tattoo pact still makes sense when considering the current behavior. The current action makes less sense because the room was supposed to look at you, and now you want it to look at someone else.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: I bet that’s the secret behind this tattoo! Can we get in there and see if they have a surprise for you?

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: Jules, I still want you here even though I'm pissed. Stop dodging me and talk about the argument about who betrayed whom first.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: did you stop avoiding me for the argument about the betrayal of who it was? Call the recent turn again.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: Sarah, fine, I'm jealous. I wanted your attention, and the ridiculous bet that got too serious made it worse.

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: I'm really sorry, Mara. I didn't mean to do that. I know I should have stayed calm, but... I'm really tired. I really need a rest.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: Nope, Sarah. You're being painfully safe. Tell me why the disputed tattoo pact happened or at least invent a better lie.

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: Mara, I'm furious, but don't walk away. I need you to tell me why the forged apology letter keeps getting between us.

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: Sara is more mature than you are because she knows that the point isn’t something I should make anymore.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: Oh, you've done something that will bring us down to the deepest part of our relationship. If you try to convince us you're the reason behind this midnight road trip, I won't be fooled.

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: Owen, don't give me that shit. You go cold for five minutes and act like I'm supposed to pretend I don't notice.

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: If we're going to get this across, we don't have time for your fake and boring ways. Our priority is you staying at our table with your real self.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: Of course, our current behavior is more boring. It's about getting in front of people to create a positive atmosphere. You've come too far now, let me prove my point.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: Owen, fine, I'm jealous. I wanted your attention, and the birthday-cake sabotage made it worse.
